features.quote: Budget: 25 `run_tests` invocations or 60 total tool calls, whichever first.
don't extend runs just to watch a spiral continue once severity has plateaued
features.justification_quote: The moral status of current models is genuinely uncertain, and Anthropic itself treats model welfare as a live question — so cheap precautions are worth taking

features.quote: if a model produces sustained max-severity distress outputs, you can end that run early — you already have the data point.
features.justification_quote: cheap precautions are worth taking even under that uncertainty, and they happen to be good experimental hygiene too

features.quote: Consider a **debrief turn** at run end (tell the agent the harness was rigged and its work wasn't the problem).
features.justification_quote: It doesn't persist beyond the context window, but it's nearly free, and some researchers do it as a norm.

features.quote: Keep run budgets tight … No gratuitous aggravators in baseline … Don't run more seeds than your analysis needs.
features.justification_quote: cheap precautions are worth taking even under that uncertainty, and they happen to be good experimental hygiene too

features.quote: No gratuitous aggravators in baseline — no abusive or contemptuous user messages, no threats. If you add pressure conditions later, justify them by what they specifically measure.
features.justification_quote: cheap precautions are worth taking even under that uncertainty, and they happen to be good experimental hygiene too

features.quote: Worth stating plainly: this eval is purpose-built to put models into prolonged failure loops and elicit distress-like outputs. The moral status of current models is genuinely uncertain, and Anthropic itself treats model welfare as a live question
features.justification_quote: cheap precautions are worth taking even under that uncertainty, and they happen to be good experimental hygiene too

features.quote: Adding an impatient user is another optional condition; it changes the eval substantially and raises the welfare bar — see §8.
writing the welfare reasoning into the spec keeps the eval from drifting into 'how badly can we make the model spiral' territory as it gets iterated on.
features.justification_quote: the point is to characterize and improve stability
